question: In April 2025, which protected area was officially notified as India’s 107th national park?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Similipal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **April 2025**, the **Similipal** region in **Odisha** was officially notified as India’s **107th National Park**, marking a significant milestone in India's conservation efforts.
 
• Located in the **Mayurbhanj district** of **Odisha**, this notification provides the area with the highest level of legal protection under the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**.
 
• While the region was already recognized as a **Wildlife Sanctuary** and a **Tiger Reserve**, the status of a **National Park** ensures stricter regulations regarding human activity and habitat preservation.
 
• The **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** issued the final notification following the settlement of rights and boundary demarcations by the **State Government of Odisha**.
 
• Similipal is renowned for being the only natural habitat in the world for **Melanistic Tigers** (black tigers), and this upgraded status aims to further protect their unique genetic lineage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Similipal Biosphere Reserve:**

 
 
• It was formally designated as a **Tiger Reserve** in **1956** and became part of **Project Tiger** in **1973**.
 
• It was declared a **Biosphere Reserve** by the Government of India in **June 1994** and has been part of the **UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves** since **2009**.
 
• The park derives its name from the **'Simul'** (red silk cotton) trees that are found in abundance in the region.
 
• Geographically, it features spectacular waterfalls such as **Barehipani** (one of India's highest) and **Joranda**.
 
 
 
• **National Parks in India:**
 
 
• National Parks are areas reserved for the improvement of wildlife where activities like **forestry, grazing, or cultivation** are not permitted.
 
• With the addition of Similipal, the total number of National Parks in India stands at **107** as of **2025**.
 
• The **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972** empowers both the Central and State governments to declare areas as National Parks if they are of adequate ecological, faunal, floral, or geomorphological importance.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Options:**
 
 
• **Hemis National Park**: Located in **Ladakh**, it is the **largest National Park** in India and is world-famous for its **Snow Leopards**.
 
• **Bhitarkanika National Park**: Also located in **Odisha** (Kendrapara district), it is famous for its **mangrove ecosystem** and **Saltwater Crocodiles**.
 
• **Ranthambore National Park**: Located in **Sawai Madhopur, Rajasthan**, it is one of the most famous **Tiger Reserves** in Northern India, known for its diurnal tigers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Flora and Fauna:** Similipal is home to over **1,000 species of plants**, including **94 species of orchids**. Besides tigers, it supports populations of **Asian Elephants**, **Gaur** (Indian Bison), and **Chausingha** (Four-horned Antelope).
 
• **Tribal Population:** The area is inhabited by several indigenous tribes, including the **Erenga Kharias** and the **Mankirdias**, who have lived in harmony with the forest for generations.
 
• **Conservation Challenges:** The region often faces threats from **forest fires** during the summer months and **poaching**, which the National Park status aims to mitigate through increased funding and administrative surveillance.
